Vakkilainen, E.K. (2006). Kraft recovery boilers - High dry solids firing. Lecture text/book manuscript, Lappeenranta University of Technology; preface dated Helsinki, 20.2.2006; publisher, year and ISBN not filled in on the title page (printed as placeholders). 250 pp.

Locators are printed chapter-page numbers (e.g. p.3-10 = chapter 3 page 10; the contents page numbering for chapter 6 does not match the body). PDF pages: chapter 1 starts PDF p.11, chapter 2 PDF p.23, chapter 3 PDF p.35. Targeted pass of a 254-page design/operation textbook with no cost data. Loaded: Table 3-7 energy balance of a 3000 tds/d, 90 bar(g)/490 degC example boiler at 65-90% dry solids (steam efficiency, steam and heat output and LHV input per t dry solids; 65-75% mapped to boiler_recovery, 80-90% to boiler_recovery-high-solids); the worked 85% DS balance (efficiency derived on HHV); typical steam conditions and sizes for two-drum, state-of-the-art and 10.4 MPa/520 degC boilers and the Iwakuni boiler; Table 1-2 black liquor gasification conversion effectiveness (reprinted from Grace and Timmer 1995). Not loaded: furnace dimensioning, fouling, corrosion, emissions chapters (non-GHG), trend figures read from charts. TRAPS: efficiency definitions (eqs 3-2 to 3-4) are images not extracted, so the Table 3-7 basis is inferred as LHV; text also cites 65 -> ~70% steam generating efficiency for the same dry-solids rise on an unstated basis; Table 2-1 net heat unit misprinted as kW/kg (kJ/kg); service unit throughout is t black liquor dry solids, not t pulp (Table 2-1: 1.68-1.78 t ds/t pulp). The held work is the "High dry solids firing" edition, not the 2005 "Principles and practice" book named in to-get.
